missionItem2_serveStatesAndConsumers.doesTheTableNeedANewState: NO. The ruling's four rows map onto the three existing states without inventing one: `value` -> `record`; `absent-verified`/`not-applicable` -> `record` (the cell's own absence IS the answer the parcel has, and the cell object travels verbatim on the wire carrying its basis/reason, so a client that wants to render 'verified absent' can); `refused`/`unaccounted` -> `refused`; no cell / malformed cell / unreadable store -> `refused`. Adding a fourth state would be a breaking change to two other repos for a distinction `record` + the cell already expresses.
missionItem2_serveStatesAndConsumers.wireChange: ADDITIVE ONLY: a new `refusal: { code, reason } | null` field on each rail, non-null exactly when `serve === "refused"`. It exists because the ruling requires a declared refusal to CARRY its reason and a MISSING or MALFORMED cell has no cell object on the wire to carry one. `serve` keeps its three states; a client that ignores unknown fields is unaffected; the two consumers that parse the response with a type cast (engine-core's client, LDT's client) are structurally tolerant of the new field because they cast `body as <its own interface>` and never validate exhaustively.
